media_strategy.selection_principle: Every visual decision flows from a data finding in analyst.json. The five channels (chart, image, video, audio, interactive_or_map) are each represented, but pacing and emphasis are tuned to the story's centerpiece: ZIP 10466 (edt_06) gets the audio sonification + scrubber + stat callout combination because that is where the data is genuinely felt rather than read.

chart.reason: Ten distinct charts: 1.4 million rows of 311 data become legible only when aggregated. Every section has a chart driven by an analyst data_table.

image.reason: One generated cinematic teaser still (a Bronx high-rise at night with one window lit far brighter than the others — a literal visual rhyme for the 10466 anomaly) plus three real-world Wikimedia reference images grounding the helicopter, brownstone-residential, and Mister-Softee paragraphs.

video.reason: An image2video animation of the teaser still: subtle dolly push toward the brightly-lit window, used as the page's first scroll-into-view element. Motion is restrained so the still composition still reads.

audio.reason: A data-bound sonification of ZIP 10466's 366-day 2024 complaint volume: each day becomes a 45 ms FM-bell pulse whose pitch and amplitude scale with that day's complaint count. The eight ≥3,000-complaint mobile-app bursts are audible as percussive slams against a near-silent baseline. This is the dataset's most surprising finding rendered into sound; readers can *hear* the spam pattern that the chart alone might not convey.

interactive_or_map.reason: (a) A Leaflet borough map of NYC with per-capita complaint rates as choropleth fill plus a single bright marker on 10466 that bridges into edt_06. (b) A synchronised scrubber on the 10466 daily timeline: as the sonification plays, a moving marker on the daily-volume bar chart tracks the day being heard.

des_teaser_image.label: Teaser hero — Bronx high-rise at midnight

content.prompt: Cinematic aerial view of a Bronx neighborhood at midnight, dense residential street with hundreds of glowing apartment windows lit yellow against deep blue night, a single brighter window on a higher floor casting a brilliant warm light into the dark, faint silhouettes of fire escapes and water towers, no people visible, editorial photojournalism, slight grain, no text in frame, 16:9

des_teaser_image.brief: A dense Bronx apartment block at night, with one window in the upper right that burns noticeably brighter than every other window — a literal visual metaphor for the central finding (one ZIP code carrying 9% of all 2024 noise complaints). The image is full-bleed at the top of the page, with no overlaid text.
des_teaser_image.rationale: The teaser image must work without explanation. A skyline at night is generic; a specific bright window inside a dense field of dim windows hints at the anomaly story before any prose is read.

des_teaser_video.label: Teaser motion — slow dolly into the lit window (image2video)

content.prompt: extremely subtle camera dolly push-in toward the brightly lit corner window of the high-rise, almost imperceptible motion, faint flickering of distant city windows in the background, no camera shake, cinematic editorial mood

des_teaser_video.brief: Six-second loopable clip: starts on the still teaser image, then slowly pushes the camera toward the brightly-lit window. Plays muted, autoplays once when scrolled into view. The page swaps in the static .jpg if video is unsupported.
des_teaser_video.rationale: We invested in a strong composition with the still; image2video keeps the composition and adds enough motion to make the page feel alive without distracting from the headline.

des_chart_01.label: Year-over-year totals — 2023 vs 2024

content.interaction: hover tooltip with exact count and per-day average

des_chart_01.brief: Two-bar chart, one for 2023 (686,283) and one for 2024 (753,275). Both bars labeled with the exact count above the bar. Bars in a muted indigo, with 2024 a half-shade brighter to signal it's the focal year.
des_chart_01.rationale: The 2023→2024 comparison is the headline of the section; a two-bar chart is the most direct way to show the +9.8% step. No need for additional encoding.

des_chart_02.label: Top 15 descriptors — Loud Music/Party dominance

content.interaction: hover tooltip with exact count + pct of all complaints

des_chart_02.brief: Horizontal bar chart, top 15 descriptors. The 'Loud Music/Party' bar at 777,689 dwarfs every other; its bar is colored a vivid orange while the rest are a soft gray. Inline value labels on every bar so the long tail is readable.
des_chart_02.rationale: The dataset's single most concentrated fact (54% of every noise complaint = one descriptor) needs the longest bar in the field to dominate everything else visually.

des_chart_03.label: Three agencies, three speeds — median + p90 response time

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows both median and p90 in human-readable units (minutes / days)

style.x_label: hours from filed to closed (log scale)

des_chart_03.brief: Three horizontal bars on a log x-axis: NYPD ~0.68h, DEP ~68h, EDC ~843h. Each bar shows the median; a lighter overlay extends to the p90. Annotated labels translate hours into 'minutes / days' for readability. The EDC bar is highlighted to underline that helicopter complaints take ~35 days to close.
des_chart_03.rationale: Linear scale would make NYPD's bar invisible. Log scale makes the three-orders-of-magnitude difference legible without exaggerating it.

des_stat_response_time.label: Stat callout — 41 minute median NYPD response

content.label: median NYPD time from complaint filed to case closed

des_stat_response_time.brief: Large 64-72px callout under the heading of edt_03, with the smaller line: '… 35 days for a helicopter complaint at EDC.' This compresses the speed-gradient finding into one easy-to-remember number.
des_stat_response_time.rationale: The 41-min median is one of the most quoted stats from the section; a callout makes it stick.

des_chart_04.label: Channel mix shift — 2023 vs 2024 by channel

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows count + pct of year's total

des_chart_04.brief: Three groups (ONLINE / MOBILE / PHONE) with two bars per group (2023 vs 2024). Online shrinks, mobile and phone both grow. The PHONE group is highlighted with a subtle outline to make the surprising +103% phone jump visible.
des_chart_04.rationale: Grouped bars let the reader see both the magnitude and the shift in one glance. The counter-intuitive PHONE growth is the section's twist, so it gets the visual emphasis.

des_chart_05.label: Borough — raw count + per-capita twin-bar

content.interaction: hover tooltip with population, raw count, per-capita

des_chart_05.brief: Two horizontal bar charts side-by-side. Left: raw complaint count (Manhattan tops). Right: complaints per 1,000 residents (Bronx tops). Shared y-axis so the reader can trace each borough from one side to the other and see the order flip.
des_chart_05.rationale: The flip from raw rank to per-capita rank is the punchline; side-by-side bars make it self-evident without extra prose.

des_map_05.label: Borough map — per-capita choropleth with 10466 marker

content.initial_state: Light-themed NYC map zoomed to all five boroughs. Each borough shaded by per-capita complaint rate (legend: 60→241 per 1k). A single bright red marker pulses softly over ZIP 10466 in the Bronx, labelled 'ZIP 10466 → next section'.
content.trigger: Hover a borough shows borough name + per-capita rate + raw count tooltip. Clicking the 10466 marker zooms in and surfaces a hint that scrolls the reader to edt_06.
content.transition: Click smoothly scrolls to edt_06 anchor and triggers the 10466 chart entrance.
content.payoff: Plants the 10466 anomaly visually before the prose explains it.
content.geo_source: Leaflet default tile layer + inline GeoJSON for NYC borough boundaries (Programmer: use the official NYC OpenData borough boundary file, or the well-known nyc-boroughs.geojson at github.com/dwillis/nyc-maps/blob/master/boroughs/nyc-borough-boundaries.geojson)

des_map_05.brief: Leaflet map of NYC. Borough polygons filled with a sequential color scale on per-capita complaint rate; legend below the map. A pulsing red dot at 10466's centroid (40.8964°N, -73.8456°W) with a tooltip 'Coming up: this one ZIP.' The map sits to the right of the twin-bar chart on wide layouts; on narrow it stacks above.
des_map_05.rationale: A choropleth makes the spatial story concrete. The 10466 marker turns the map into a hand-off device to the next section's reveal.

des_stat_10466.label: Stat callout — 8.97% from one ZIP

content.label: of all 2024 NYC noise complaints came from a single Bronx ZIP code

des_stat_10466.brief: Massive 96px stat anchoring the top of edt_06. The sub-label is two lines, italic serif, with '67,571 of 753,275, ZIP 10466, ~62,000 residents.'
des_stat_10466.rationale: The section is the spine of the entire piece; the number deserves the page's biggest typographic moment.

des_chart_06.label: ZIP 10466 — top 10 single-day bursts, stacked by channel

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows date, total, channel breakdown. Click 'Play sonification' button below the chart triggers des_audio_10466 and moves a small marker over the chart in sync.

des_chart_06.brief: Horizontal stacked bars for the 10 noisiest single days in 10466, with each bar split into mobile / online / phone segments. The mobile slice is nearly the entire bar in every case (≥99% of complaints on every top-10 day). The top bar (2024-09-15, 4,952 complaints) is annotated with the line 'one every 17.4 seconds'.
des_chart_06.rationale: Stacked bars make the channel concentration (the story is mostly a mobile-app story) visible at a glance, on top of the absolute volume.

des_audio_10466.label: Sonification — 10466's 366 days of 2024 as percussive pulses

content.why_audio: The chart shows magnitudes; the sound shows *rhythm*. Most days are inaudibly quiet (median = 12), then a burst day arrives like a slam. Hearing the year unfold in 16 seconds makes the spam pattern visceral in a way no static chart can.
content.trigger: Click the 'Play 10466's year' button under des_chart_06. Hard rule: never autoplay.
content.ui_form: chart-synced sonification — a vertical scrubber line sweeps across a small 366-day bar chart of 10466's 2024 daily counts while the audio plays. The bar currently being heard pulses red. Pause/play and a mute toggle are visible.

content.prompt: Each day → 45 ms FM bell at a pitch logarithmically mapped from complaint count (low pitch = quiet day, high pitch = burst day), amplitude scaled by sqrt(count/5000). Silent on zero-complaint days. 22 kHz mono, 16-bit, ~16.5 seconds total.

content.fallback: If audio is muted/unsupported the small 366-day bar chart is fully readable on its own; the play button shows a disabled state with the tooltip 'audio unavailable in this browser'.
content.novelty_note: Not a tone card — the audio is bound 1:1 to a paired chart, and the scrubber forces the reader to see the same data they hear.

des_audio_10466.brief: 16-second percussive sonification of ZIP 10466's daily complaint volume across all of 2024. Paired with a 366-day bar chart (data from ana_26) whose bar pulses red as each day is heard. Designed to make the eight ≥3,000-complaint mobile-app bursts audible as percussive slams against a near-silent baseline.
des_audio_10466.rationale: This dataset has 366 ordered values with extreme outliers — exactly the kind of sequence sonification adds genuine meaning to.

des_chart_07.label: Helicopter complaints — monthly, 2023 vs 2024

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows month + each year's count + delta

des_chart_07.brief: Two-line chart, x = month (Jan-Dec), y = helicopter complaints. The 2023 line is brighter and visibly higher in nearly every month; the 2024 line sits flat near 2,500. December 2023's spike to 8,724 is annotated with a small callout.
des_chart_07.rationale: A line chart shows the 51% YoY drop as a clear separation rather than a single number, and reveals the December anomaly that the prose mentions.

des_asset_helicopter.label: Reference photo — helicopter landing at East 34th Street Heliport
des_asset_helicopter.brief: Editorial-style photo of a HeliFlite executive helicopter landing at East 34th Street — one of the two city-owned heliports targeted by the 2025 Helicopter Oversight Act. Placed to the right of the helicopter chart on wide layouts.
des_asset_helicopter.rationale: The story isn't about helicopters in the abstract; grounding the section in a real heliport photo helps the reader picture where the noise is coming from.

des_chart_08.label: Hour-of-day — weekday vs weekend, per-day rate

content.interaction: hover tooltip with hour + both series counts + ratio

des_chart_08.brief: Two filled-area line chart. X-axis = hour 0..23. Weekday line sits below; weekend line peaks dramatically at 22:00–23:00. The 11 PM weekend annotation calls out the 1.95× ratio. Light orange = weekend, light blue = weekday.
des_chart_08.rationale: Two overlapping line/area series make the late-night weekend lift instantly visible, and the chart is the natural anchor for the section's claim that 11 PM Sunday is the loudest hour.

des_chart_09.label: NYPD residential resolutions — 0.28% summons rate

content.interaction: hover tooltip with bucket name, count, pct

des_chart_09.brief: Single horizontal stacked bar (100% width) showing the five NYPD residential resolution buckets. The dominant 'no evidence' (40%) and 'responded — took action' (46%) segments are in cool grays; 'issued a summons' (0.28%) is a sliver of bright red on the far right, annotated with a callout 'one in 360 calls'.
des_chart_09.rationale: A 100% stacked bar makes proportional dominance immediate; the visual punch is the tiny red sliver alongside the dominant gray.

des_stat_summons.label: Stat callout — 0.28% summons rate

content.label: of NYPD residential noise complaints ended with a summons or violation issued

des_stat_summons.brief: Inline pull-quote-sized stat (60-72px): '0.28% — about 1 in 360 calls.' Sits at the top of edt_09, above the stacked-bar chart.
des_stat_summons.rationale: The number is more quotable than the chart; the callout makes it the section's headline.

des_asset_softee.label: Reference photo — Mister Softee ice cream truck
des_asset_softee.brief: Wikimedia photo of a classic blue-and-white Mister Softee ice cream truck. Placed in the second half of edt_09 alongside the paragraph about the 15 violations in 2,805 complaints.
des_asset_softee.rationale: A real photo of the offending vehicle makes the absurdity of the 1-in-187 enforcement ratio land harder than text alone.

des_chart_10.label: Borough year-over-year — diverging bar

content.interaction: hover tooltip shows 2023 count, 2024 count, delta, pct change

des_chart_10.brief: Diverging horizontal bars showing each borough's 2023→2024 percent change. Bars extending right (positive) in warm orange (Bronx +51%, Staten Island +6%, Brooklyn +2%); bars extending left (negative) in cool blue (Manhattan -3%, Queens -2%). The Bronx bar is annotated with 'subtract 10466 → +9.5%'.
des_chart_10.rationale: A diverging bar makes the up/down split visceral and lets the +51% Bronx bar dominate, then the annotation immediately attributes most of it to ZIP 10466.

des_asset_brownstone.label: Reference photo — Bed-Stuy residential block
des_asset_brownstone.brief: Wikimedia photo of Tompkins Avenue between Willoughby and Hart, Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn — a classic NYC residential block where 'Loud Music/Party' complaints originate. Sits to the right of the descriptor chart on wide layouts.
des_asset_brownstone.rationale: Grounds the abstract complaint_type breakdown in a real residential streetscape.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial; deep indigo background, cream typography, one accent color (a warm coral red) reserved for the 10466 / 0.28% callouts and the helicopter chart annotation
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: visual-first hook (full-bleed teaser video + image fallback), then a strict text-then-chart pattern through edt_02–edt_05, then edt_06 (the turn) breaks the rhythm with a full-width stat callout, a stacked chart, a paired sonification scrubber, and no body text continuity, then text-then-chart resumes for edt_07–edt_10, then a quiet text-only close
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Avoid the standard chart-card chart-card rhythm. The audio sonification is the unique visual+sonic moment and should be the only place a play button appears. No third-party sound clip embeds; no decorative ambient noise. The map and the diverging YoY bar are the only two non-bar/non-line shapes — keep the rest of the chart language deliberately restrained so the sonification scrubber and the per-capita map stand out.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: stat callouts at 72px-96px serif italic for emphasis; pull quotes in 22px italic with a left border; section dividers are 1px hairlines in muted indigo; charts use 14px labels and 12px tick labels for readability on mobile; teaser video is full-bleed at the top with an aspect-ratio: 16/9 wrapper to prevent layout shift
